overall_notes: Lesson 5 capstone integrates C3.1+C3.2 with explicit cross-references to Lessons 1-4 (concurrent reading L1, writing L2, bug detection L3, fixing L4). Trap is the no-bug-plant misconception cited to Brennan & Resnick (2012, 'New Frameworks for Studying and Assessing the Development of Computational Thinking'); recovery_moves branch by three diagnostics (A: clean code without bugs, B: plants but can't articulate, C: plants but partner can't find). NO-PAPER alternative is provided in differentiation (chalk on floor or floor tape with partner walking through the code physically). Buzz + Patch deliver the capstone refrain 'TRACE it, FACE it, REPLACE it! FIND it, ALTER it, TEST it!' which the class chants 3x in the consolidation. Children invent their own concurrent code, plant deliberate bugs, swap, and compare strategies in whole-class share. Worksheet Parts 1-3 map to the three success criteria; Part 4 (reflection on which bug type was easiest) is a metacognitive transfer task rather than a rote repeat. All six categories clear Level 4. Pass.
